source.excerpt: Philosophy is questions that may never be answered.
trail: The complete inspected Quote Investigator investigation identifies a J. J. Hahn Usenet signature dated 16 January 1995 as its earliest located match. Hahn is a candidate, not a proven creator.
QI reproduces Dennett’s 2006 epigraph with an Anonymous credit and gives chapter 1, section 4, page 17. That supports genuine use by Dennett while refuting an assumption of original authorship.
The publisher confirms Breaking the Spell’s subject and 2006 ebook publication, but the publisher catalog does not reproduce the epigraph.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Breaking the Spell examines religion as a natural phenomenon that can be investigated. An epigraph contrasting philosophy and religion fits that project, but Dennett supplied it as an anonymous quotation. The source trail therefore separates his documented use from the still unresolved question of who composed it.

schema.claimReviewed: Daniel Dennett originated “Philosophy is questions that may never be answered. Religion is answers that may never be questioned.”
schema.faqAnswer: Daniel Dennett used the saying in Breaking the Spell (2006) but explicitly credited Anonymous. Quote Investigator documents the same formulation in a 1995 Usenet signature by J. J. Hahn; the ultimate creator is unconfirmed.
schema.verdictNote: The false claim is original authorship by Dennett. His use of the quotation is genuine, and J. J. Hahn remains a candidate rather than an established creator.
